Now, I'm not your normal animal lover. I'd be down for eating human stew, long as the human was on board with the whole process and was compensated in a way they agreed to. But I do think there's a solid argument for giving your food some respect on its way to your plate.

I also think if people were more cognizant of how similar we really are, they'd be less keen to be "carnivores". Leather used to be seen as "magical" and still having the soul of the animal that produced it in it. Meat tastes delicious as a reward for a challenging hunt.

In other words, I think the only cows I should be eating are the ones that are my friends. Those ones I know had a good life before reaching my plate. Slaughterhouses are brutal, and if they were a necessity I could get over it, but they're not. It's easy to get enough protein and fat without meat (the meat turned plants into that protein and fat in the first place), so it's pointless pain for an unhealthy "luxury" that isn't even that great because 1) Slaughterhouses don't produce top quality meat and 2) When you have it all the time, it stops being a luxury, the rarity is part of what makes meat so delicious in the first place.

I personally just feel really attuned with the "humans are animals" side of things. Which both means we're capable of as much (or more) 'harshness' (what's the difference between edward gein and an orangutang that bites a woman's hands off?) and capable of much more for having the faculties we do (there are very few animals that have the capacity to care for an injured animal of a different species, the only two I know of offhand are dolphins and humans, maybe elephants do it too?). We really are "barbarians with culture" in a lot of respects, I feel.
